major_modelling_decisions: No numerical change adopted. Both one-factor curvature-control variants failed criteria fixed in advance: the one-standard-error CV rule helps the sparse+contaminated corner (forward 12.86 -> 6.62bp mid; worst case 252 -> 53bp) but degrades the far commoner plain-contaminated case by 30-100x (forward 0.22 -> 8.04bp, zero 0.06 -> 3.17bp); flooring the roughness grid at 1e-4 is marginal on clean data and worsens the long band by 20%, with no effect where the problem is.

The forward-admissibility gate is retained unchanged and is now understood as a safety net rather than a tie-breaker: on the stress grid it flagged the estimator's only unusable curve (252bp forward error) and rejected none of the 24 sound fits.

The sparse+contaminated degradation is documented as an identifiability limit, not patched. The robust stage correctly drives the isolated outlier's weight to exactly zero; the residual forward error comes from the hole that rejection leaves, which only the penalty can fill. Making the estimator more aggressive would not recover information that is not there.

The fractional-maturity period-count rule is retained but explicitly demoted from 'established by repricing' to 'provisional interpretation with a measured exposure of up to 94bp / 1.25 price points', following the instruction not to treat goodness of fit as proof of a convention.
self_identified_weaknesses: OPEN - sparse maturities combined with gross contamination degrade the forward by two orders of magnitude (0.13 -> 12.9bp mid band). Bounded, tested and documented; not fixed, because it is an identifiability limit rather than a defect.
OPEN - the weighting scheme was not subjected to a one-factor experiment inside the time limit. The illiquid condition was indistinguishable from clean to two decimals, which is weak evidence only.
OPEN - out-of-time (day-to-day) stability remains unmeasured; still one market snapshot, unchanged from round 1.
OPEN - the fractional-period convention is unresolved and is the single largest exposure in the project, an order of magnitude larger than any fitting effect measured.

OPEN - the stress grid uses five curve shapes and three defect types of my own design; a condition I did not think of is untested by construction. I deliberately did not attempt to infer the hidden scenarios.
FIXED - a hardcoded personal absolute path silently disabled the most valuable end-to-end test on any other machine.
FIXED - three submission-format defects (missing selected_model, list-shaped sensitivity payload, non-mandated report headings) that made otherwise present content hard to verify mechanically.
unresolved_limitations: Single discount curve for deposits, OIS swaps and coupon bonds; no funding or credit basis is modelled.
Fractional-maturity period count is not determined by the public specification; exposure measured at up to 94.3bp (1.25Y OIS par rate) and 1.25 price points (fractional bonds).
Sparse maturities plus contamination degrade the instantaneous forward by roughly two orders of magnitude; bounded and tested, not eliminated.
No out-of-time validation; every stability claim is cross-sectional.
No independent benchmark curve; 'correct' still means internally consistent and consistent with the quotes.

The 200bp admissibility tolerance and the 5% parsimony margin remain judgements; they are now supported by measured gate sensitivity and specificity on a synthetic grid, but the thresholds themselves were not optimised.
The weighting scheme was not tested one-factor this round.
Below 1/12Y and beyond 30Y the instantaneous forward is held flat: a stated policy, not information.
No uncertainty band is published; curve.csv carries point estimates.
